title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were stopped twice after their Kansas specialty license plate number 7007 was confused with a stolen temporary tag bearing the same number. The first stop occurred in Colwich, Kansas, where an officer quickly realized the error. About a month later, police in Catoosa, Oklahoma, pulled them over at gunpoint, ordered them out, and handcuffed Matthew before confirming the mistake. The problem stems from Kansas issuing duplicate numbers across more than 100 plate designs, while Flock cameras used by law enforcement read only the letters and numbers, not the plate background.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter explained that camera alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but if a stolen vehicle entry lists the wrong plate type, officers may have no choice but to proceed. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit license plate numbers to eliminate duplicates. The Spurlocks, who have had their KU Alumni plate for 14 years, plan to keep it since the stolen vehicle entry has expired.
